title: skilldrop skill manifest
$comment: RFC-0029. This shape lived only as prose in AGENTS.md, so the one authoritative statement of what a manifest is was a paragraph a contributor had to read and obey. It is now data. Checked by hand-rolled stdlib code in validate.py — skilldrop ships zero runtime dependencies and this file must not become a reason to add `jsonschema`.

name.description: Kebab-case. Must equal the folder name AND the SKILL.md frontmatter name — the triple-match in golden rule 1.

description.description: The most-read string in the skill. Use-case-first: what it does, then the trigger phrases an agent matches on. Must match the SKILL.md frontmatter description.

required.description: Vars the skill cannot work without, e.g. FIGMA_TOKEN.

optional.description: Vars that change behaviour but do not block.

related.description: Undirected: every sibling this SKILL.md references, in either direction. validate.py enforces the sync both ways.

handoff.description: RFC-0028. The directed companion to `related`. Every `to` must also appear in `related`.

to.description: A skill folder name. Never this skill.

when.description: The condition under which the hand-off fires.

purpose.description: What the target does with what it receives.

fallback.description: What to do when the target is not installed. Required — this is what makes an advisory hand-off degrade in a stated way instead of dead-ending.

tier.description: Abstract and provider-neutral. Never a vendor model name — the provider map in model-routing.json is the only place concrete models live. Must agree with this skill's entry there.

rationale.description: One sentence: why this tier fits what the skill does.

install.description: Human-readable install lines for a skill with runtime deps.

hooks.description: RFC-0006. Only for loop-shaped skills that benefit from event automation; artifact generators carry none.

action.description: A real skill folder this hook points at.
